http_semantics.note: The rejection itself uses the correct status class (400 format error, empty-body envelope with status.error text). The defect direction is the inverse of 2xx-masking: a schema-valid, documented-optional-field-omitted request is WRONGFULLY rejected with 400. Phenomenon is illegal-rejection semantics although the in-log verdict labels it Type1_IllegalSuccess — label/phenomenon mismatch recorded for the auditor. Also note the claim's parenthetical 'all accepted spellings exhausted' is inaccurate: only one spelling was attempted for M3 (no alt form in the script), and per source a context-explicit spelling ({"discover":{"target":1,"context":null}} or with a pair) does parse — the primary observation (documented minimal shape 400) is nonetheless genuine and fully covered by this chain.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: POST /collections/{c}/points/query body -> QueryRequest (#[serde(flatten)] internal) -> QueryRequestInternal.query: Option<QueryInterface> -> QueryInterface untagged [Nearest(VectorInput) | Query(Query)] -> Query untagged [.. Discover(DiscoverQuery) ..] -> DiscoverQuery { discover: DiscoverInput } -> DiscoverInput { target: VectorInput (untagged, Id(PointIdType) accepts the bare u64 1 — proven live by M2 positive=[1,2] and byid_lookup's {"query": 301} both 200), context: Option<Vec<ContextPair>> } where context's #[serde(with = "MaybeOneOrMany")] WITHOUT #[serde(default)] makes the field wire-MANDATORY per serde_derive 1.0.228 expr_is_missing_fn; omitting context therefore fails DiscoverInput deserialization, the untagged Query/QueryInterface layers swallow the inner error and surface the generic expecting-message with HTTP 400. The schemars-generated OpenAPI face still advertises context as optional (Option type; MaybeOneOrMany's JsonSchema OneOrMany enum includes a _None alternative), so docs and parser disagree — the schema-valid minimal discover is treated exactly like a bogus variant. Same-file contrast (Prefetch.prefetch = default+with works when omitted) and cross-face contrast (dedicated DiscoverRequestInternal plain-Option accepts target-only, in-chain 200) show the omission-tolerance was implemented elsewhere deliberately and is missing here.
source_grounding.outcome_note: Over-strict deserialization rather than missing validation: the source fails to honor the documented optionality of DiscoverInput.context (serde(with) without serde(default)) on the unified query face, so a schema-valid domain member (discover, target-only) is wrongfully rejected. NOT marked by_design_in_source: no comment/docstring/maintainer marker declares context mandatory on this face (v3.4 decision-2 tightened), the same file shows the authors add #[serde(default)] precisely when omission must work (Prefetch.prefetch, QueryGroupsRequestInternal.prefetch), the dedicated discover face accepts target-only, and no in-tree test covers the omission path — bare 'it behaves this way' is exactly what the rules forbid calling by-design.
